nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n > 0$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label of $i$ with offset $s$ is at most $2n$.
nodes.title: Cyclic labels do not exceed the number of vertices

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n > 0$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label $c$ of $i$ with offset $s$ satisfies $1 \le c \le 2n$.
nodes.title: Range of the cyclic labels

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $s$ and every position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$, the cyclic label of $i$ with offset $s$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Cyclic labels are positive

nodes.summary: Let $n > 0$ be a natural number and number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. Then the cyclic label with offset $0$ of the position $0$ (the vertex $v_1$) is $1$.
nodes.title: The cyclic label of the first position with offset zero

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $s$ be natural numbers. Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. The cyclic label with offset $s$ of the position $i \in \{0, \dots, 2n - 1\}$ is $((i + s) \bmod 2n) + 1$.
nodes.title: Cyclic labeling of the ladder perimeter

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $s$ be natural numbers. Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n - 1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. The offset $s$ gives a consecutive cyclic prime labeling of the ladder when $n > 0$ and, for all positions $i, j \in \{0, \dots, 2n - 1\}$ that are adjacent in the ladder graph, the cyclic labels of $i$…
nodes.title: Consecutive cyclic prime labeling of the ladder

nodes.summary: Number the vertices of the ladder $P_n \times P_2$ along its perimeter by $0, 1, \dots, 2n-1$, with $v_k$ at position $k - 1$ and $u_k$ at position $2n - k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. Two positions $i, j \in \{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$ are adjacent when $j \equiv i + 1 \pmod{2n}$ or $i \equiv j + 1 \pmod{2n}$ (neighbours along the perimeter cycle), or when $i + j = 2n - 1$ (the rung joining $v_k$ and $u_k$).
nodes.title: Adjacency in the ladder graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
